body:
Nothing actionable turned up in today's scan: the opportunity finder returned zero cross-platform arbitrage candidates. That's a normal outcome — most scans find nothing, and today is one of those quiet days rather than a sign the scanner is broken.

The price ladder itself does tell a story, though. Kalshi's gold at year-end settle-above contracts price $4,300 at a 0.68 bid and $4,400 at 0.61, while its August 31 settle-above strikes show roughly even odds sitting near $4,400–4,450. On Polymarket, the low-touch contracts for $3,800 and below are quoted at just 1-2 cents, essentially treated as dead. Together these imply the market expects spot gold to be trading well north of $4,300, consistent with the historic run gold has been on: futures went from roughly $2,600 at the start of 2025 to a record above $4,300 by mid-October, as gold has once again captured the financial world's attention, surging to an unprecedented high above $4300 per ounce on October 17, 2025, before experiencing a sharp, albeit temporary, dip later the same day. One analyst noted $4,000 an ounce seemed far-fetched at the start of the year as gold entered 2025 near $2,800 an ounce (CBS News). So the unusually high strike prices on the board aren't a data glitch, they're the market pricing off a genuinely record rally.

Worth flagging for readers comparing the two platforms directly: Kalshi's gold contracts settle on the spot price at one specific moment (a settle market), while Polymarket's touch-low/touch-high contracts pay out if gold crosses that level at any point during the window (a touch market). That structural difference means a wide-looking price gap between similarly-labeled contracts often reflects different resolution rules rather than a genuine mispricing — which is also likely why the scanner found no clean arbitrage today despite the divergent-looking quotes.
headline: No arbitrage found today, but gold contract pricing reflects the metal's record rally

sources.title: CBS News: What's driving the gold price surge
